clue.text: Promotional work to bring joy to church dignitary

parts.note: PR, public relations, is promotional work
to elate is to bring joy to

explanation.surface: A publicity campaign designed to cheer up a senior clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking cleric such as a bishop or archbishop.

clue.text: Attendant trailed by worker in procession

indicators.note: trailed by means the attendant comes first with the worker behind

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A page boy followed by a labourer marching in a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a public show or parade, a procession of costumed figures.

clue.text: Greek character in Eastern province shows weariness

indicators.note: in means the Greek letter sits inside the province

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person living in an eastern region looks tired.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek character is a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom or tiredness of spirit.

clue.text: A downfall affecting moguls?

parts.note: moguls suggests tycoons facing ruin, but moguls are also bumps on a ski slope, buried by snow falling down

explanation.surface: Seems to describe the collapse of business tycoons' fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow sliding down a mountainside, smothering the slopes.

clue.text: Aspire in turn to be around clubs for long period

indicators.note: to be around means the reversed word surrounds the clubs letter
in turn means the word for aspire is turned around to read backwards

parts.note: to hope is to aspire
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Ambitions, taken in turn, gather around golf clubs over a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' makes EPOH from HOPE; C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era, a long and distinct span of history.

clue.text: Element in rebellion is enjoying acclaim

indicators.note: Element in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a rebellion is enjoying popular approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise someone is to treat them as a celebrity, heaping praise on them.

clue.text: See ordinary detective with younger relative

parts.note: lay means non-professional, ordinary as opposed to expert
a private eye is a detective
a son is a younger family member

explanation.surface: A plain-clothes investigator working alongside a junior family member.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay eyes on something is idiom for catching sight of it.

clue.text: Working couple initially rejected being televised?

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: initially rejected means the first letter of the word for couple is thrown out

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A working duo turned down at first for a television appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is being broadcast, on television or radio.

clue.text: Popular side developed around place that's being debated

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the word for place
developed means the letters of side are worked into a new form

parts.note: to put is to place

explanation.surface: A popular team has grown up around a disputed ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' reads as a team in the surface but is just anagram fodder, signalled by 'developed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in dispute is one still being argued over.

clue.text: Firm cutting money desperately makes saving

indicators.note: cutting means the firm letters cut into the shuffled money
desperately suggests the letters of money are in wild disorder

parts.note: CO, company, is a firm

explanation.surface: A company desperate to cut costs makes savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective but stands for a company; 'makes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy is thrift, the careful saving of money or resources.

clue.text: Trees as an object of study?

definitions.text: Trees as an object of study?

parts.words: Trees as an object of study?
parts.note: suggests botany or forestry, but the trees are family trees, and their study is the tracing of ancestry

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a science devoted to studying trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Genealogy is the study of family lineage, set out in charts called family trees.

clue.text: Arab citizen with no small love of sound

indicators.note: with no means the letter for small is dropped from the word for the citizen

parts.note: a Saudi is a citizen of Saudi Arabia
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: An Arab national who loves sound, as in audio equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio, as a noun, refers to recorded or transmitted sound.

clue.text: Something picked in dry outfit for woman

indicators.note: in means the picked thing sits inside the dry outfit

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is an organisation whose members stay dry, off alcohol
a nit, a louse egg, is picked out of hair

explanation.surface: Something chosen in a plain costume for a woman to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is a woman's first name; crosswords often define names this way.

clue.text: Stop here possibly to take in variable conjuror's expression

indicators.note: to take in means the shuffled letters swallow the variable
possibly signals that the letters of stop here could be arranged another way

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A sign asking you to stop here and absorb some variable quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram, and 'to take in' sets the variable inside the rearranged letters, after the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: Hey presto is the exclamation a magician makes as a trick is revealed.

clue.text: Persevering figure is given account with financial promises

parts.note: ten is a number, or figure
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A determined person keeps a figure, an account and some debts in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacious means holding firmly to a purpose, as a persevering person does.

clue.text: Treat obtained by one in uncluttered entrance to eatery

indicators.note: in means the obtained-and-one letters go inside the word for uncluttered

parts.note: neat means tidy, uncluttered
got means obtained
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: entrance to means only the opening letter of eatery is used

explanation.surface: A restaurant treat collected at a tidy front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat' is a verb here, as in treating with an enemy, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat with someone is an old sense of to bargain or negotiate terms.

clue.text: Causes or events of special significance

definitions.meaning: to occasion is to bring about
an occasion is a notable event or celebration

explanation.surface: Reasons for, or else important happenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasions are both causes, as in giving occasion, and special events like weddings.

clue.text: Examine royal house with gold stolen in Surrey's borders

indicators.note: in means the shortened royal house goes between those border letters
borders means only the first and last letters of Surrey are used
with gold stolen means the heraldic word for gold is taken away

parts.note: the Tudors were an English royal house
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Investigate a royal family whose gold was taken within the county of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county just south of London. The Tudors are the royal house, not the Stuarts or Windsors.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something is to examine it carefully.

clue.text: Cox, perhaps, sits with nice blue on bottom of boat

indicators.note: blue, as in feeling out of sorts or turned blue, signals the letters of sits and nice are rearranged
bottom of means the last letter of boat, its base in a down entry

explanation.surface: A man called Cox sits with a sad-looking companion in the bottom of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Cox suggests a boat's coxswain or an apple, but here it is the physicist Brian Cox; 'blue' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Professor Brian Cox, the physicist and broadcaster, is an example of a scientist.

clue.text: Obsession followed by the Parisian music maker

indicators.note: followed by means the obsession comes first and the French article after it

parts.note: a bug is a craze or obsession, as in the travel bug
le is the French for the, as a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: A passion for French music-making.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a brass instrument, so something that produces music.

clue.text: Cover group of corporate bigwigs on the rise

parts.note: a company's board is its body of directors
up means rising

explanation.surface: Executives whose profits are rising hide the evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To board up a window or door is to cover it with planks.

clue.text: Assured fine don works in college tutorials, principally

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters sit inside the college letter and the tutorials initial
principally means only the first letter of tutorials is taken
works means the letters of fine don are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A self-assured academic who does well in tutorials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' turns FINE DON into ONFIDEN, which goes 'in' between C and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Confident means sure of oneself, assured.

clue.text: One scavenging rubbish by yard is near to collapse?

parts.note: a totter is a rag-and-bone man, one who goes totting, salvaging rubbish

explanation.surface: A scavenger by a rubbish yard who looks ready to fall over.
explanation.walkthrough: TOTTER as a scavenger is British slang: totting is collecting saleable scrap from rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottery means shaky and unsteady, so likely to fall.

clue.text: A new piece of advice regarding early part of meal

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint, a piece of advice
as to means regarding or concerning

explanation.surface: A fresh tip about how to begin a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is an Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables served before the main course.

clue.text: Seeded food is something checked by a medic

definitions.meaning: edible seeds such as lentils and beans
a doctor checks your ..., the heartbeat felt at the wrist

explanation.surface: Beans, or what a doctor feels at your wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulse names both edible legume seeds and the rhythmic throb of the arteries.

clue.text: Old fool limiting current place for refreshment

indicators.note: limiting means the fool word encloses the current symbol

parts.note: an ass is a fool
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An elderly idiot restricting the flow to a watering hole.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile, watered spot in a desert where travellers refresh themselves.

clue.text: Bishop's neighbour announced time for rest?

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: on a chessboard the knight starts next to the bishop

explanation.surface: Someone living next to a bishop declares it is bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is a chess piece, not a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is when most people sleep, so it is a time for resting.

clue.text: Rat that's a feature in a garden

definitions.meaning: to rat or ... is to inform on someone; a ... is an informer
..., the lawn, is a common garden feature

explanation.surface: A rodent that is part of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASS is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass means both an informer and the lawn that covers a garden.

clue.text: Slow utterance or line by one in custody on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means the letters are seen as in a mirror, read backwards

parts.note: a ward is a person, often a minor, in someone's legal custody

explanation.surface: A prisoner, thinking back, speaks slowly or offers a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a lazy, drawn-out manner of speaking.

clue.text: Former student struggling in a test is difficult to change

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: struggling means the letters of in a test are in disarray

explanation.surface: An ex-pupil who is struggling in an exam will not change his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate means stubborn, unwilling to change one's mind.

clue.text: Look by English ship for titled female

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
SS, steamship, is a standard ship prefix

explanation.surface: Gazing at an English vessel in search of a noblewoman.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress is a woman holding a title of nobility in her own right or by marriage.

clue.text: Meet the requirements of doctor first, say, right away

indicators.note: doctor, as a verb, means to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
away means the letter for right is removed

explanation.surface: Seeing the doctor first, say, straight away, to meet requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal; 'away' drops R from FIRST SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy conditions is to fulfil or meet them.
